title: Quiche Lorraine
subtitle: The classic French tart of smoked lardons and cream in a short pastry shell
excerpt: Quiche Lorraine has three components: short pastry, smoked lardons, and a rich cream and egg custard. The pastry must be blind-baked until fully set before the custard goes in, or the base will be wet. The custard should be barely trembling when the quiche comes out of the oven and will firm completely as it cools.
sourceNotes: Quiche Lorraine originated in the Lorraine region of France. The canonical version contains no cheese; gruyere is a later addition common in UK and international versions. The recipe documented here follows the traditional form: blind-baked short pastry, smoked lardons, and a cream-heavy savoury custard.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked and cooled. Reheat from frozen at 160 degrees Celsius for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Quiche is at its best on the day of baking, served at room temperature. It keeps refrigerated for 3 days and reheats well.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 170 degrees Celsius for the filled quiche. Blind bake the pastry at 190 degrees Celsius first. Fan oven: reduce each by 15 degrees.

glossaryTerms.definition: A mixture of eggs, cream, and milk that sets to a silky solid in the oven. The ratio matters: all double-cream with no milk gives a rich, almost dense set; adding whole milk lightens the texture. More yolks give a yellower, more velvety set. Quiche Lorraine uses a cream-heavy, all-yolk custard.

content.text: The key to a set, non-soggy quiche is a fully blind-baked pastry case. The
is poured into a hot case with the oven immediately reduced; this gives the custard a gentle heat from the start and sets the edges before the centre warms through.

Rub the butter into the flour and salt until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to bring the dough together. Press into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Roll out on a floured surface and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 15 minutes. Blind bake at 190 degrees Celsius for 20 minutes with baking paper and baking beans, then remove the beans and paper and bake for a further 8 minutes until the pastry is pale gold and dry throughout.

items.prepNote: grated; optional but traditional in many versions

content.text: Fry the lardons in a dry pan over medium heat until they render their fat and turn lightly golden. Drain on paper and scatter over the hot pastry case.
Whisk together the egg yolks, whole egg, cream, milk, and salt. Scatter the gruyere over the lardons if using. Pour the custard slowly into the hot pastry case.

Reduce the oven to 170 degrees Celsius and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Remove from the oven and allow to cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.
